items.q: A 48-year-old multiparous woman presents with progressively heavy, prolonged menstrual bleeding for 8 months. Her cycles occur every 28 days with 8 days of heavy bleeding and clots. Pelvic examination is unremarkable, and ultrasound shows a normal uterus with an endometrial stripe of 12 mm. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
o: Immediate insertion of a 52 mg LNG-IUS
items.exp: According to ACOG and FIGO guidelines, any woman aged 45 years or older presenting with abnormal uterine bleeding must undergo endometrial biopsy to exclude endometrial hyperplasia and adenocarcinoma prior to initiating definitive medical or hormonal therapy.
r: Correct. Age >= 45 with AUB mandates endometrial biopsy as the initial investigative step.
Incorrect. LNG-IUS is excellent medical therapy, but histological exclusion of malignancy must precede it.
Incorrect. Tranexamic acid treats symptoms but fails to assess the mandatory risk of endometrial neoplasia.
Incorrect. Laparoscopy does not evaluate the uterine cavity or endometrium.
items.kp: Any woman aged 45 or older presenting with abnormal uterine bleeding must undergo endometrial biopsy to exclude malignancy.

items.q: Under the FIGO PALM-COEIN classification system, which of the following is classified as a non-structural etiology of abnormal uterine bleeding?
items.exp: In the PALM-COEIN system, PALM represents structural etiologies (Polyp, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, Malignancy/hyperplasia), whereas COEIN represents non-structural etiologies (Coagulopathy, Ovulatory dysfunction, Endometrial, Iatrogenic, Not otherwise classified).
r: Correct. Ovulatory dysfunction belongs to COEIN (non-structural category).
Incorrect. Adenomyosis belongs to PALM (structural).
Incorrect. Polyp belongs to PALM (structural).
Incorrect. Leiomyoma belongs to PALM (structural).
items.kp: PALM represents structural lesions; COEIN represents non-structural, functional, and systemic causes of AUB.

items.q: Which medical therapy provides the greatest reduction in menstrual blood loss for women with idiopathic heavy menstrual bleeding?
o: Cyclic oral medroxyprogesterone acetate for 10 days/month
items.exp: The 52 mg LNG-IUS is the most effective medical treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding, reducing measured menstrual blood loss by 70% to 95% within 6 to 12 months. Short-course luteal progestins (10 days/month) are ineffective for HMB.
r: Correct. The 52 mg LNG-IUS achieves up to 90-95% reduction in menstrual blood loss, superior to all oral regimens.
Incorrect. Tranexamic acid achieves a 40-55% reduction.
Incorrect. Cyclic 10-day progestins do not reliably reduce blood loss and are not recommended for HMB.
Incorrect. NSAIDs achieve approximately 25-35% reduction.
items.kp: The 52 mg LNG-IUS is the most effective medical therapy for heavy menstrual bleeding, reducing blood loss by up to 95%.

items.q: A 52-year-old postmenopausal woman with obesity presents with a single episode of vaginal spotting. Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrates an endometrial thickness of 8 mm. What is the definitive management step?
items.exp: Postmenopausal bleeding requires prompt histological evaluation. An endometrial thickness > 4 mm on transvaginal ultrasound in a postmenopausal patient carries an elevated risk of endometrial cancer (~10%) and mandates outpatient endometrial biopsy.
r: Correct. Postmenopausal bleeding with endometrial stripe > 4 mm mandates histological sampling.
Incorrect. Reassurance is dangerous because postmenopausal bleeding carries a 10% risk of carcinoma.
Incorrect. Estrogen is contraindicated in uninvestigated vaginal bleeding.
Incorrect. Hormonal therapy without histological diagnosis is malpractice.
items.kp: Postmenopausal bleeding with endometrial thickness > 4 mm on ultrasound requires mandatory endometrial biopsy.

items.q: What is the primary mechanism of action of tranexamic acid when used in the treatment of heavy menstrual bleeding?
items.exp: Tranexamic acid is a synthetic lysine analogue that competitively blocks the lysine binding sites on plasminogen molecules, preventing its conversion to plasmin and thereby inhibiting fibrin degradation (antifibrinolytic action).
r: Correct. Tranexamic acid competitively inhibits plasminogen activation, stabilizing fibrin clots in endometrial vessels.
Incorrect. It has no hormonal or steroidogenic activity.
Incorrect. Vasoconstriction is mediated by prostaglandins and endothelin, not tranexamic acid.
Incorrect. Cyclooxygenase inhibition is the mechanism of NSAIDs.
items.kp: Tranexamic acid is a synthetic antifibrinolytic that competitively blocks plasminogen activation to reduce bleeding.

items.q: An endometrial biopsy in a 54-year-old woman with AUB demonstrates atypical endometrial hyperplasia (endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia). What is the concurrent risk of co-existing invasive endometrial adenocarcinoma on definitive hysterectomy?
items.exp: Multiple landmark prospective Gynecologic Oncology Group (GOG) studies have established that approximately 40% (range 35-43%) of women with a preoperative biopsy diagnosis of atypical endometrial hyperplasia are found to have concurrent invasive endometrial adenocarcinoma upon hysterectomy.
r: Correct. Approximately 40% of patients with atypical hyperplasia harbor concurrent invasive carcinoma.
Incorrect. 2% corresponds to non-atypical simple hyperplasia.
Incorrect. 10% significantly underestimates the risk confirmed by GOG trials.
Incorrect. 90% is overly high.
items.kp: Atypical endometrial hyperplasia carries an approximately 40% concurrent risk of invasive adenocarcinoma on final surgical pathology.

items.q: A 16-year-old girl presents with severe menorrhagia since menarche, requiring blood transfusion. She reports frequent epistaxis and easy bruising. Her mother had severe postpartum bleeding. What is the most likely underlying diagnosis?
items.exp: Severe menorrhagia starting at menarche associated with personal or family history of mucosal bleeding (epistaxis, bruising, postpartum hemorrhage) is the classic presentation of an inherited bleeding disorder, most commonly von Willebrand disease (AUB-C in PALM-COEIN). Up to 20% of adolescents hospitalized for severe AUB have an underlying coagulopathy.
r: Correct. von Willebrand disease is the most common inherited bleeding disorder causing severe menorrhagia at menarche.
Incorrect. ITP causes isolated thrombocytopenia without positive family history of inherited bleeding.
Incorrect. Factor V Leiden is a thrombophilic mutation causing thrombosis, not bleeding.
Incorrect. PCOS causes anovulatory irregular cycles, but mucosal bleeding and positive family history indicate coagulopathy.
items.kp: Severe menorrhagia at menarche with a history of mucosal bleeding strongly indicates von Willebrand disease (AUB-C).

items.q: Which diagnostic imaging modality has the highest sensitivity for distinguishing an intracavitary endometrial polyp from a submucosal leiomyoma?
items.exp: Saline infusion sonohysterography (SIS) distends the uterine cavity with sterile saline, allowing high-resolution transvaginal sonographic differentiation between flexible, echogenic endometrial polyps and firm, hypoechoic, myometrium-derived submucosal fibroids with over 95% sensitivity.
r: Correct. Saline infusion sonohysterography accurately delineates intracavitary contour and base of attachment.
Incorrect. Transabdominal ultrasound has poor resolution for small intracavitary lesions.
Incorrect. Pelvic CT has poor soft tissue resolution for endometrial intracavitary architecture.
Incorrect. HSG identifies filling defects but cannot distinguish polyp tissue from fibroid tissue.
items.kp: Saline infusion sonohysterography (SIS) is the investigation of choice for distinguishing endometrial polyps from submucosal fibroids.

items.q: What is the recommended initial management for a 50-year-old perimenopausal woman with atypical endometrial hyperplasia who has completed childbearing and is medically fit?
o: Oral high-dose megestrol acetate for 6 months
Insertion of 52 mg LNG-IUS with observation
items.exp: Definitive management of atypical endometrial hyperplasia in women who have completed childbearing is total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, due to the 40% risk of underlying concurrent adenocarcinoma and malignant progression. Progestin therapy is reserved strictly for patients desiring fertility preservation or unfit for surgery.
r: Correct. Hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy is the standard definitive treatment.
Incorrect. Medical progestin therapy is second-line, reserved only for fertility preservation or high surgical risk.
Incorrect. Endometrial ablation is contraindicated because it prevents future histological surveillance and can trap cancer.
Incorrect. LNG-IUS alone is not first-line when childbearing is complete and patient is surgical candidate.
items.kp: Total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy is the definitive treatment for atypical endometrial hyperplasia.

items.q: Which medication is specifically contraindicated in patients with abnormal uterine bleeding who have an active history or high risk of venous thromboembolism?
items.exp: Combined oral contraceptive pills contain ethinylestradiol, which promotes hepatic synthesis of procoagulant clotting factors and significantly increases venous thromboembolism risk. They are contraindicated in women with prior DVT, pulmonary embolism, or active thrombophilia. Progestin-only methods (LNG-IUS) do not increase VTE risk.
r: Correct. Estrogen-containing combined pills are contraindicated in patients with history of VTE.
Incorrect. LNG-IUS does not increase VTE risk and is safe in women with thromboembolic history.
Incorrect. Tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic but can be used with caution; combined estrogen carries higher baseline risk.
Incorrect. NSAIDs do not promote venous thrombosis.
items.kp: Estrogen-containing contraceptives are contraindicated in women with abnormal bleeding and active or prior venous thromboembolism.
